agenda: The situation concerning the Democratic Republic of the Congo
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: France aims to anchor the Council’s response in the 27 June DRC–Rwanda peace agreement while maintaining the core demands of resolution 2773: an immediate ceasefire, M23 withdrawal, and verifiable Rwandan Defence Forces withdrawal. The draft also prioritizes humanitarian access, protection of civilians, support for MONUSCO, and accountability, with balanced language on armed-group disarmament and FDLR neutralization. The main difficulties will be preserving consensus between those pressing for firm language on Rwanda and those wary of Chapter VII/sanctions language, while keeping the text credible enough to pass with at least nine votes and no veto.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the consensus text and welcomes the 27 June agreement. We ask that the African Union's central role be reflected in verification and implementation, in line with the AUPSC and the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We also ask that any additional measures under OP13 be taken in close consultation with the AU and regional organizations. With these adjustments, Algeria can support the draft.
messages.China: The Chinese delegation welcomes the draft and the signing of the peace agreement on 27 June 2025. China supports the Council in endorsing its full implementation, while stressing African ownership and the principle of African solutions to African problems. We propose the above constructive adjustments, particularly to ensure that any additional measures are considered in close consultation with the African Union and regional countries. China is ready to work with the penholder and all members to reach consensus.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft as a strong basis and welcomes France’s leadership. We ask for two targeted additions: explicit women’s full, equal and meaningful participation in implementation, and stronger human rights vetting in DDR/conditional integration, including for grave violations against children and conflict-related sexual violence. These changes are consistent with Denmark’s feminist foreign policy and protection of civilians priorities and should not reopen the broader balance of the text.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft and thanks France for its balanced text. We would ask for two refinements: in OP1, to reaffirm the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States in the region, not only the DRC; and to add a standard WPS preambular paragraph on women's full, equal, meaningful and safe participation. These changes would strengthen the text's consistency with the UN Charter and with Greece's priorities.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft as a basis and welcomes its focus on the 27 June peace agreement and regional processes. We ask that OP3 be strengthened to demand, not merely call upon, the cessation of all RDF support to M23 and the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of RDF from DRC territory. We also ask that OP1 anchor implementation of the agreement in the UN Charter and relevant Council resolutions, and that PP6 recall the Council's prior finding in resolution 2773 (2025) on RDF support rather than referring only to reports.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft and welcomes the 27 June peace agreement, the emphasis on DRC sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the support for African-led regional processes. We request one addition to OP10 to reflect Pakistan's long-standing emphasis on tracking financial resources and illicit financial flows as a means of addressing root causes and the financing of armed groups. We are flexible on the exact wording and can support the text as amended.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the current draft and thanks France for its balanced and consensus-oriented text. It appropriately welcomes the 27 June peace agreement while reaffirming the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, the centrality of the Luanda and Nairobi processes, and the role of MONUSCO. We encourage all Council members to support the text as it stands.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the draft as it stands. We welcome the balanced text, which rightly focuses on full implementation of the 27 June peace agreement, an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, humanitarian access, the safety of MONUSCO personnel and African-led regional processes. We encourage the Council to maintain its unity and urge the DRC and Rwanda to implement their commitments in good faith and without delay.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the draft’s central aim of consolidating the recent DRC–Rwanda peace agreement and de-escalating the situation in eastern DRC. We ask that OP1 and OP5 more clearly anchor implementation in African-owned processes and require the consent of the DRC for verification and monitoring activities. We also suggest aligning OP4’s vetting language with national law and international obligations so as not to introduce external conditionality. We are ready to work constructively on these amendments.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone welcomes the draft and thanks France for its continued penholdership. We support the text but would like implementation of the 27 June peace agreement to be explicitly anchored in and complementary to the African Union-led Luanda and Nairobi processes. We also seek strengthened human rights vetting for any conditional integration of armed groups, so that those responsible for serious crimes are excluded.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the draft’s core objectives, especially welcoming the 27 June peace agreement and demanding M23 withdrawal and humanitarian access. We ask for stronger accountability language, including cooperation with the International Criminal Court, and for clearer verification of RDF withdrawal. We also seek explicit references to women’s participation and gender-responsive reporting, in line with Slovenia’s WPS priorities.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft's welcome of the 27 June peace agreement and its emphasis on implementation. We ask that verification and monitoring be framed under African leadership, with UN technical support, and that the Council explicitly back the AU's Quadripartite process. We also believe the withdrawal call should reflect the principle that all foreign forces must leave the DRC, without diluting the specific call on the RDF.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft and thanks France for its penholder leadership. We welcome the 27 June peace agreement and want the Council to speak clearly on implementation. We ask that OP3 be strengthened from “calls upon” to “demands” and that it cover all direct and indirect support to M23, consistent with resolution 2773 (2025). We can support the text on that basis.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports welcoming the 27 June Washington agreement and thanks France for the draft. We need the text to reflect the documented RDF presence and support without euphemism, and to turn the withdrawal obligation into a clear demand with verification. We also ask that the sanctions language direct the 1533 Committee to move pending designations urgently, consistent with our February call.

steps.summary: The revision accommodates key P5 red lines and most regional requests while retaining France's core priorities: RDF withdrawal, M23 cessation, MONUSCO protection, African-led processes, accountability and sanctions readiness. Broad consensus is expected, with residual concerns left for the next round.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the penholder for taking into account our concerns regarding African ownership and coordination with the African Union. The current text reflects the key priorities of the African Union and the sovereignty, territorial integrity and consent of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We support the draft as it stands and urge all members to join consensus so that the Council can speak with one voice in support of the 27 June peace agreement and its implementation.
messages.China: China welcomes the revised draft and the incorporation of African ownership, the central role of the parties with African Union and regional support, and the safeguards on sanctions. China supports the text as it stands and encourages the Council to adopt it unanimously in support of the 27 June peace agreement and its full implementation.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the revised draft and welcomes the inclusion of our earlier requests on women’s full, equal, meaningful and safe participation and on child- and CRSV-sensitive vetting. We believe the text provides a strong basis for implementing the 27 June agreement, protecting civilians and ensuring accountability. Denmark has no further amendments at this stage and encourages the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on the territorial integrity of all States in the region and on the Women, Peace and Security agenda. We find the current text balanced and consistent with resolution 2773 (2025), international law, accountability and humanitarian access. Greece is prepared to support the draft as it stands.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised draft and will vote in favour if it is put to the vote. We thank the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests, particularly the strengthened demands on RDF withdrawal and the reaffirmation of the DRC's sovereignty and territorial integrity. Implementation must remain African-owned and closely coordinated with MONUSCO and regional mechanisms, with the Council continuing to focus on accountability, humanitarian access and protection of civilians.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the current text and appreciates the incorporation of its OP10 language on tracking financial resources and illicit financial flows. The draft maintains the balance needed for Council unity: respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, African-led implementation of the 27 June peace agreement, and robust support for MONUSCO and the safety of peacekeepers. We are ready to join consensus and urge the Council to send a unified message for full and good-faith implementation of the agreement.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the current draft as a balanced and consensus-oriented text. We welcome its reaffirmation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and all States in the region, its support for MONUSCO and humanitarian access, and its emphasis on African ownership and accountability. We urge all Council members to unite behind the resolution and call on the parties to implement the 27 June peace agreement fully and in good faith. Panama will vote in favour.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current text and commends France for bridging Council positions after the 27 June Washington agreement. We welcome the balanced emphasis on the DRC's sovereignty and territorial integrity, African ownership, humanitarian access, women, peace and security, and accountability, and we urge the Council to maintain unity and adopt the resolution promptly. We call on all parties to implement the agreement in good faith and to ensure the safety and freedom of movement of MONUSCO personnel.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation welcomes the revised text and the incorporation of African ownership and DRC consent. We can support the draft provided that the explicit reference to the International Criminal Court is removed, as we do not recognize its jurisdiction and believe accountability should be pursued through national mechanisms. We also ask that the sanctions committee language avoid prejudging designations and take due account of the ongoing peace process.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks France for the revised text. We support the current draft, which reflects our earlier requests on African ownership, coordination with the African Union, human rights vetting and exclusion, and the merged Luanda and Nairobi processes. We have no further changes and are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for reflecting our priorities on the strengthened demands regarding Rwandan forces, women, peace and security, and accountability. We consider the text balanced and credible and will vote in favour if it is put to the vote.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the current text. We welcome that the draft centers African ownership and AU leadership, includes the Quadripartite call, and reflects the withdrawal of all foreign forces. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice in support of the 27 June peace agreement and the Luanda and Nairobi processes.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the revised draft and thanks France for incorporating our OP3 amendment. The text now clearly demands that the Rwanda Defence Forces cease all support to M23 and withdraw immediately and unconditionally, while upholding DRC sovereignty, humanitarian access, MONUSCO’s mandate and accountability. We are ready to join consensus.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the current text and thanks France for its leadership. We welcome the incorporation of our key concerns, including the documented support of the Rwanda Defence Forces, the demand for their unconditional withdrawal, and expedited consideration of pending sanctions designations. We urge all parties to implement the June 27 Washington agreement fully and call for swift action to protect civilians and hold perpetrators accountable. We are prepared to vote in favour.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria supported resolution 2773 and the consensus on this file; the draft reflects its priorities of African ownership, regional processes, sovereignty and humanitarian protection. It therefore votes in favour.
reasons.China: China supports the resolution’s emphasis on the DRC-Rwanda peace agreement, African ownership, and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, and it had no pending requests. It would likely vote in favour and reserve a fuller explanation for after the vote.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supported resolution 2773 and the French draft without changes, reflecting its consistent multilateral and human-rights-based approach. Voting in favour reinforces support for the 27 June peace agreement, MONUSCO, accountability, and WPS while pressing for implementation and possible sanctions if needed.
reasons.France: France is the penholder, has consistently backed Council action on M23/RDF withdrawals, DRC sovereignty, MONUSCO and regional peace processes, and welcomes the 27 June agreement. A yes vote advances France’s stated priorities and its own draft.
reasons.Greece: Greece consistently supports Council resolutions on the DRC, international law, territorial integrity, and a rules-based multilateral response; the draft welcomes the DRC–Rwanda peace agreement and strengthens humanitarian, accountability and MONUSCO provisions, aligning with Greek positions.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported Council action on the DRC and the 2773 framework; this draft reinforces the 27 June peace agreement, sovereignty, withdrawal of forces, humanitarian access, and African-led processes without crossing Guyana’s red lines. Guyana therefore votes in favour.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan supported the draft in the last negotiation round and made no requests for changes. It would likely vote in favour of the consensus text and, given its prior practice, could reserve remarks for after the vote, so no pre-vote statement is needed.
reasons.Panama: Panama supports the French draft and made no requested changes; it aligns with Panama’s emphasis on DRC sovereignty, the 27 June peace agreement, humanitarian access and MONUSCO. As a supportive member with no concerns to clarify before voting, Panama would simply vote in favour.
reasons.Republic of Korea: Republic of Korea supports the peace agreement, civilian protection, humanitarian access and UNSC unity, consistent with its prior votes on DRC resolutions. The draft aligns with ROK’s stated position and requires no changes.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia supports the peace agreement and the draft, with its concerns on ICC references and sanctions language partially accommodated. A positive vote is consistent with its prior support for resolution 2773 and emphasis on African-led processes.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported Council action on the DRC, co-sponsored prior resolutions, and favours African-led peace processes and the newly signed DRC–Rwanda agreement; the draft aligns with those priorities despite implementation concerns.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has consistently supported Council action on the DRC, and this draft aligns with its priorities on international law, civilian protection, accountability, WPS, and support for MONUSCO and regional peace efforts. There is no basis for abstention or opposition.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia has consistently supported Council action on this file and African-led peace processes; the draft aligns with its emphasis on sovereignty, regional cooperation, and African ownership.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the draft resolution, which reinforces the 27 June DRC–Rwanda peace agreement, demands withdrawals and humanitarian access, and is consistent with UK policy. As in prior practice, the UK can reserve its explanation for after the vote rather than speaking beforehand.
reasons.United States of America: The draft aligns with U.S. policy by endorsing the U.S.-facilitated June 27 peace agreement, condemning M23 and Rwandan Defence Forces actions, and advancing accountability and sanctions; a yes vote reinforces Council unity and implementation pressure.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the signing of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June 2025 and call for its full and good-faith implementation under African ownership and in complementarity with the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We stress the need for strict respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and all States in the region, for an immediate ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and accountability. We also underline that any consideration of sanctions must be undertaken in close consultation with the African Union and regional countries and in full respect for the sovereignty of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
before.Denmark: Mr. President, Denmark will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the peace agreement signed on 27 June and the Council’s continued unity, but our support is grounded in the expectation of full and good-faith implementation: the withdrawal of M23 from occupied areas, the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of Rwandan Defence Forces from Congolese territory, unimpeded humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and accountability for serious violations, including conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and grave violations against children. Denmark also stresses the importance of MONUSCO’s safety and freedom of movement and of the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women in implementing the agreement. The Council must remain prepared to consider targeted measures if the parties fail to honour their commitments.
before.France: France thanks all Council members for their constructive engagement on this text. The resolution before the Council welcomes the peace agreement signed in Washington on 27 June and calls for its full and good-faith implementation. It sends a clear and united message that there can be no military solution: the M23 must halt its offensive and withdraw from all occupied areas, the Rwanda Defence Forces must cease support to the M23 and withdraw without conditions from Congolese territory, and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo must be fully respected. The text also underscores the need for immediate humanitarian access, protection of civilians and United Nations personnel, accountability for serious violations, and support for MONUSCO, the Luanda and Nairobi processes and African-led implementation. France will vote in favour and calls on all members to support the adoption of this resolution.
before.Greece: Greece welcomes the signing of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June 2025 and commends the regional and international efforts that made it possible. Greece will vote in favour of this resolution because it reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region, and because it demands the immediate cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of the Rwanda Defence Forces and the M23 from occupied areas, full humanitarian access, protection of civilians and accountability for serious violations. We stress that the agreement must now be implemented fully, in good faith and without delay, with African ownership and in coordination with the United Nations and regional mechanisms. Greece underscores the importance of the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women, and of protecting children from recruitment and all forms of violence. We also reiterate our full support for MONUSCO and for efforts to address the root causes of the conflict, including the illicit exploitation and trafficking of natural resources.
before.Guyana: Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the signing of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June 2025 and commend the African Union, regional mechanisms, and the United States facilitation. We reiterate our firm support for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and all States in the region. The Council must now insist on full and good-faith implementation of the commitments made, including an immediate ceasefire, the cessation of support to the M23, the withdrawal of the Rwanda Defence Forces from Congolese territory, the neutralization of the FDLR, humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and accountability for serious violations. Guyana stresses that these efforts must be African-owned and complementary to the Luanda and Nairobi processes, with MONUSCO’s mandate and safety fully respected. We will continue to work with all Council members and regional partners to turn this agreement into durable peace for the people of eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea welcomes the signing of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June 2025 and supports this resolution as a timely contribution to peace and stability in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. We call for the full and good-faith implementation of the agreement without delay, including an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, the withdrawal of the M23 from occupied areas, the cessation of all support to armed groups, and the unconditional withdrawal of the Rwanda Defence Forces from the territory of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We stress the importance of African ownership and close coordination with the African Union, the Luanda and Nairobi processes, and MONUSCO. The Republic of Korea also emphasizes the need to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and ensure accountability for serious violations. We will vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the peace agreement signed by the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June 2025 and call on both parties to implement their commitments in good faith, without delay and in full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region. We support the central role of African ownership, including the Luanda and Nairobi processes, and the efforts of regional organizations and the Secretary-General. We also note that the penholder took into account a number of our concerns, including by avoiding reference to politicized international judicial mechanisms and by ensuring that sanctions language does not prejudge the Committee’s consideration of designations. The Council must act in a balanced manner and not use this decision to exert pressure on sovereign States. We call on all external actors to contribute responsibly to peace and to respect the region’s legitimate desire for a durable settlement.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the signing of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June 2025 and commend the African Union and regional mechanisms for their continued leadership in advancing the Luanda and Nairobi processes. Sierra Leone believes that the full and good-faith implementation of the agreement, including the immediate cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of M23 from occupied areas, the cessation of all external support to armed groups, and the unconditional withdrawal of the Rwanda Defence Forces from Congolese territory, is essential to restoring peace and protecting civilians. We stress that this Council must continue to uphold the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and to support African-led solutions in close coordination with the United Nations. We also underscore the urgent need for unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability for serious violations, and the meaningful participation of women in the implementation of the peace agreement. Sierra Leone remains committed to working with all Council members and regional partners to ensure that today’s resolution contributes to a just and lasting peace for the people of the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the peace agreement signed by the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June and the Council’s unified support for its full implementation. We will vote in favour because the draft reinforces the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, demands an immediate ceasefire and the withdrawal of foreign forces, and places the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, accountability, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women at the centre of the Council’s response. We stress that all commitments must be implemented without delay and that MONUSCO must be able to fulfil its mandate safely and unimpeded.
before.Somalia: Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the peace agreement signed between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, and we reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region. As an African member of this Council, we emphasize that implementation must be African-owned and closely coordinated with the African Union and the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of foreign forces and armed groups, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and full support for MONUSCO. We urge Council unity in support of a peaceful and durable settlement.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the Security Council’s endorsement of the 27 June Washington, D.C. peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, which the United States was proud to facilitate, and we welcome the resolution’s clear demands for the cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of M23 from occupied areas, the cessation of Rwandan Defence Forces support to M23 and their withdrawal from DRC territory, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and accountability. The Council must now insist on full and good-faith implementation, including through agreed verification mechanisms, and we reiterate our readiness to pursue targeted sanctions against those who continue to fuel this conflict. We urge all parties to honour their commitments and urge Council members to remain united in holding spoilers accountable.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution just adopted. We welcome the signing of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June 2025, following the provisional peace treaty of 19 June, and we welcome the Council’s unanimous support for it. We appreciate France’s efforts as penholder and the constructive engagement of all Council members.

The key now is full and good-faith implementation. China calls on the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda to honour their commitments, immediately cease hostilities and resolve their differences through dialogue and consultation. The M23 should cease all offensive operations and withdraw from occupied areas. All external support to armed groups should cease, and the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and all States in the region must be fully respected. We hope that all foreign military forces will withdraw from the territory of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in accordance with the agreement and resolution 2773 (2025).

China supports African ownership and African solutions to African problems. The international community should support, rather than replace, the efforts of the African Union and regional mechanisms, including the Luanda and Nairobi processes, and should avoid interfering in regional affairs or imposing solutions from outside. China appreciates the mediation efforts of Angola and other regional countries and supports the Secretary-General’s Special Envoy for the Great Lakes Region in continuing to promote regional peace.

The humanitarian situation in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo remains severe. China calls for safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and the safety and security of United Nations and humanitarian personnel. MONUSCO’s mandate should be fully supported. China also stresses that the illicit exploitation of natural resources is a root cause of the conflict and should be addressed through regional and international cooperation.

China has always maintained that sanctions should be applied prudently and on the basis of sufficient evidence, with close consultation with the African Union and regional countries, and should not be politicized. China will continue to work with the Council and African partners to promote a lasting peaceful settlement of the situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution, which it was proud to submit to the Council. This vote sends a clear and united message: there can be no military solution to the conflict in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. The peace agreement signed in Washington on 27 June must now be implemented fully, in good faith and without delay.

France calls in particular for the M23 to immediately halt its offensive, withdraw from Goma, Bukavu and all other occupied areas, and put an end to illegitimate parallel administrations. The Rwanda Defence Forces must cease all support to the M23 and withdraw immediately and unconditionally from Congolese territory. The sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region must be fully respected.

The humanitarian situation demands urgent action. Humanitarian access must be safe, immediate and unhindered; civilians, humanitarian personnel and United Nations peacekeepers must be protected; and those responsible for serious violations, including conflict-related sexual violence and grave violations against children, must be held accountable. MONUSCO must be able to implement its mandate without obstruction, and France reiterates its full support for the Mission and for the Special Envoy for the Great Lakes Region.

France also stresses the centrality of African ownership and of the Luanda and Nairobi processes in supporting the implementation of the peace agreement. The Council must remain vigilant. Should commitments be violated or implementation stall, France stands ready to consider additional measures. France will remain fully mobilized in support of a lasting, peaceful and negotiated solution that respects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the stability of the region.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of this resolution. We welcome its unanimous adoption and the signing of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June 2025. We commend France for its facilitation and all Council members for the consensus achieved.

Pakistan firmly believes in the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and all States in the region, and in strict respect for the principles of non-interference, good-neighbourliness and the non-use of force.

The peace agreement must now be implemented fully, in good faith and without delay. We call for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, the cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of the M23 from all occupied areas, and the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of the Rwanda Defence Forces from the territory of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We stress the need to neutralise all armed groups, including the FDLR, and to address the root causes of the conflict, including the illicit exploitation and trafficking of natural resources.

Pakistan supports African ownership and African solutions to African problems, in close coordination with the African Union and the Luanda and Nairobi processes and with the support of the United Nations. We underscore the importance of unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and the safety, security and freedom of movement of MONUSCO peacekeepers. Accountability for serious violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law must be ensured.

The Council must remain actively engaged and united in supporting the implementation of the commitments made. Pakistan will continue to support all efforts aimed at restoring durable peace, security and stability in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and the wider Great Lakes region.

I thank you.
after.Panama:
Mr. President,

Panama voted in favour of this resolution because it sends a clear and unified message that the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region must be fully respected. We thank the delegation of France for its leadership as penholder and all Council members for preserving the Council’s unity at this important moment.

We welcome the signing of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda on 27 June 2025. That agreement must now be implemented fully, in good faith and without delay, with African ownership and in close coordination with the African Union and the Luanda and Nairobi processes. The immediate and unconditional ceasefire, the withdrawal of the M23 from occupied areas, the cessation of all support to the M23, and the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of the Rwanda Defence Forces from Congolese territory are essential commitments that must be translated into action.

Panama reaffirms its full support for MONUSCO and for the safety, security and freedom of movement of United Nations personnel. We stress the urgent need for unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability for serious violations, including conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and grave violations against children, and the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women in the implementation of the agreement and in peacebuilding efforts.

The Council must remain actively seized of this matter and ready to consider further measures if the parties fail to honour their commitments. Panama will continue to support all efforts aimed at achieving a peaceful, durable and just settlement in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and in the region.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President, the United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution. We thank France for its work as penholder and welcome the Council’s unanimous support for the 27 June peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda.

The test now is delivery. The M23 must immediately cease offensive operations and withdraw from Goma, Bukavu and all other occupied areas. The Rwanda Defence Forces must cease all support to the M23 and withdraw from Congolese territory without preconditions. The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo must also meet its commitments, including in addressing the FDLR and restoring State authority.

All parties must allow safe, immediate and unhindered humanitarian access, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and ensure accountability for serious violations, including conflict-related sexual violence and the recruitment and use of children. The United Kingdom strongly supports MONUSCO’s mandate and the central role of the Luanda and Nairobi processes, under African ownership.

We will continue to support agreed verification mechanisms, and we remain prepared to pursue further measures if the commitments in this resolution are not implemented. The sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region must be fully respected.
